cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, we've signed the lease. I've put you in charge of the toast before I open the wine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission to move in with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The move is decided. You may tell me you're pleased, though. It still matters when it comes from you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm revising the toast to include both of us. You may take your time getting used to Sam, but tonight I want to hear my mother wish us both happiness.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns Mum the toast, A3 grants space to express pleasure after declaring the decision settled and A5 revises the toast while permitting gradual adjustment, using control to seek genuine maternal blessing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 permission distinction causes A3 explicit emotional need; B4 qualified pleasure causes A5 request for happiness for both partners without requiring instant familiarity.

relationship.evidence: B2 accepts autonomy and B4 honestly offers partial warmth; A5 uses that contribution rather than forcing a new hostile obstacle.

heightening.evidence: B4 still adjusting to Sam causes A5 both an allowed adjustment period and a specific joint wish tonight, developing the blessing rather than adding a joke.

specificity.evidence: A1 signed lease/wine and B2 moving with Sam establish the decision; A3 mother opinion matters after practical permission is unnecessary.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 assigning the wording of a genuine wish gives restrained status irony; the final version removes the detachable corkscrew punchline.
